html:
Thuringia is a region in the middle of Germany. In 1815 it was not one state but a cluster of small ones: the Ernestine duchies of Saxon origin, such as Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach, Saxe-Gotha, Saxe-Coburg and Saxe-Meiningen, plus the lands of the Schwarzburg and Reuss families.

The splintering began in 1485, when the house of Wettin divided its lands, and went on as the Ernestine line kept splitting between heirs. Small as they were, these courts mattered. Frederick the Wise protected Martin Luther at the Wartburg castle near Eisenach. Weimar drew Goethe and Schiller and became the centre of German classical culture. The Coburg family supplied kings to Belgium, Portugal and Britain.

The states joined the German Confederation and later the German Empire. After the monarchies fell in 1918, seven of them merged in 1920 into the state of Thuringia. Weimar gave its name to the Weimar Republic, whose assembly met there in 1919.
